title: Senso-ji Temple
summary: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 645 AD, with the iconic Kaminarimon gate and a lively approach street.
access: 5-minute walk from Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line)

title: Yanaka Ginza
summary: An old-town shopping street with local snacks and a relaxed, un-touristy atmosphere.
access: 7-minute walk from Nippori Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
summary: Fresh seafood, street food stalls, and knife shops in Tokyo's famous market district.
access: 2-minute walk from Tsukijishijo Station (Toei Oedo Line)

title: Shimokitazawa Backstreets
summary: Vintage shops and standing bars packed into narrow streets, popular with local students rather than tour groups.
access: 1-minute walk from Shimokitazawa Station (Odakyu / Keio Inokashira Lines)

title: Meiji Jingu Shrine
summary: A forested shrine at the edge of Harajuku, built for Emperor Meiji, where a ten-minute walk through 100,000 donated trees replaces the city noise with birdsong.
access: 1-minute walk from Harajuku Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Meiji Jingu & Harajuku walking tour

title: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
summary: The famously chaotic pedestrian crossing where up to 3,000 people cross at once — best viewed from the Shibuya Sky observatory or a window seat in a nearby cafe.
access: Directly outside Shibuya Station's Hachiko Exit (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Takeshita Street
summary: A narrow pedestrian street packed with crepe stands, pastel fashion boutiques, and character goods stores — the birthplace of Harajuku's youth fashion scene.
access: 1-minute walk from Harajuku Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Ginza
summary: Tokyo's most polished shopping district, lined with flagship department stores and architect-designed boutiques; on weekend afternoons the main avenue closes to cars entirely.
access: 1-minute walk from Ginza Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza/Marunouchi/Hibiya Lines)

title: Akihabara Electric Town
summary: Multi-storey electronics and anime shops stacked on top of each other, plus retro arcades and maid cafes — the center of Tokyo's otaku culture.
access: 1-minute walk from Akihabara Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Akihabara anime & retro gaming tour

title: Ueno Park & Ueno Zoo
summary: A sprawling public park that turns into one of Tokyo's most popular cherry blossom spots each spring, home to Japan's oldest zoo, a lotus pond, and several museums.
access: 2-minute walk from Ueno Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Tokyo National Museum
summary: Japan's oldest and largest museum, holding samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, and Buddhist sculpture spanning thousands of years across several galleries inside Ueno Park.
access: 10-minute walk from Ueno Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Tokyo National Museum guided tour

title: Ameyoko Market
summary: A loud, crowded market street under the train tracks near Ueno, selling everything from fresh fish and dried snacks to discount sneakers and imported spices.
access: 1-minute walk from Ueno Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Ryogoku Sumo District
summary: Home to the Ryogoku Kokugikan sumo arena and dozens of sumo stables — visit during a tournament month to hear the crowd roar, or just wander past chanko-nabe restaurants year-round.
access: 1-minute walk from Ryogoku Station (JR Sobu Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a sumo tournament ticket experience

title: Tokyo Skytree
summary: At 634 meters, one of the tallest towers in the world, with two observation decks looking out over the entire Kanto plain on a clear day.
access: Directly connected to Tokyo Skytree Station (Tobu Skytree Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Tokyo Skytree observation deck tickets

title: teamLab Planets
summary: A barefoot, walk-through digital art museum where visitors wade through knee-deep water and mirrored rooms full of projected flowers and light.
access: 5-minute walk from Shin-Toyosu Station (Yurikamome Line)

title: Roppongi Hills & Mori Art Museum
summary: A glass-tower complex with a contemporary art museum on the 53rd floor, an open-air sky deck, and one of Tokyo's busiest nightlife districts at street level.
access: 3-minute walk from Roppongi Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya/Oedo Lines)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Mori Art Museum & Tokyo City View tickets

title: Kagurazaka
summary: A former geisha district of stone-paved alleys and hidden French bistros tucked behind an unassuming shopping street — one of the few areas in central Tokyo that still feels like old Edo after dark.
access: 1-minute walk from Kagurazaka Station (Tokyo Metro Tozai Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kagurazaka food walking tour

title: Nakano Broadway
summary: A slightly worn 1960s shopping arcade that has quietly become a mecca for vintage toys, manga, and collectible figures — an Akihabara alternative favored by longtime collectors.
access: 5-minute walk from Nakano Station (JR Chuo Line)

title: Jiyugaoka
summary: A leafy residential neighborhood known for boutique homeware shops and some of Tokyo's most photogenic patisseries, popular with locals rather than tour groups.
access: 1-minute walk from Jiyugaoka Station (Tokyu Toyoko Line)

title: Osaka Castle & Osaka Castle Park
summary: A rebuilt 16th-century castle with a museum inside its keep, set in a large park that turns pink with cherry blossoms every spring.
access: 10-minute walk from Osakajokoen Station (JR Osaka Loop Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Osaka Castle admission with guided tour

title: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden Observatory
summary: Two towers joined by an open-air rooftop walkway 173 meters up, offering one of the best sunset views in the city.
access: 7-minute walk from Osaka Station (JR lines)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Umeda Sky Building observatory tickets

title: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
summary: Japan's longest covered shopping arcade at 2.6 kilometers, with around 600 small shops selling everything from takoyaki to secondhand kimono.
access: Directly connected to Minami-Morimachi Station (Osaka Metro Tanimachi Line)

title: Osaka Tenmangu Shrine
summary: A shrine dedicated to the god of learning, best known for hosting the Tenjin Festival every July, one of Japan's three largest festivals.
access: 3-minute walk from Minami-Morimachi Station (Osaka Metro Tanimachi Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Osaka shrines & Tenjin district tour

title: Nakanoshima
summary: A slim river island lined with rose gardens, riverside cafes, and a mix of century-old and brand-new museum buildings, right in the middle of the business district.
access: 3-minute walk from Naniwabashi Station (Keihan Nakanoshima Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Nakanoshima Museum of Art tickets

title: Kuromon Ichiba Market
summary: Known as "Osaka's Kitchen," a 580-meter covered arcade of about 150 stalls selling grilled seafood, wagyu skewers, and fruit you can eat on the spot.
access: 2-minute walk from Nippombashi Station (Osaka Metro Sennichimae Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kuromon Market food-tasting walk

title: Hozenji Yokocho
summary: An 80-meter stone-paved alley of old-school bars and restaurants tucked just behind Dotonbori's neon, centered on a small moss-covered temple statue.
access: 5-minute walk from Namba Station (Osaka Metro Midosuji Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Dotonbori & Hozenji night food tour

title: Amerikamura (America Town)
summary: A compact grid of streets packed with secondhand fashion, streetwear boutiques, and record shops — Osaka's answer to Harajuku, centered on a small park nicknamed "Triangle Park."
access: 5-minute walk from Shinsaibashi Station (Osaka Metro Midosuji Line)

title: Namba Grand Kagetsu
summary: A working comedy theater that runs manzai stand-up and Yoshimoto Shinkigeki slapstick plays daily — even without fluent Japanese, the physical comedy carries the room.
access: 3-minute walk from Namba Station (Osaka Metro Midosuji Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Namba Grand Kagetsu comedy show tickets

title: Universal Studios Japan
summary: A major Hollywood-themed amusement park with a dedicated Super Nintendo World zone and a Wizarding World of Harry Potter area, popular with families and ride enthusiasts alike.
access: 5-minute walk from Universal-City Station (JR Yumesaki Line)

title: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
summary: One of the world's largest aquariums, built around a central tank that recreates the Pacific Ocean, home to whale sharks that visitors view from multiple floors as they spiral downward.
access: 5-minute walk from Osakako Station (Osaka Metro Chuo Line)

title: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
summary: One of the largest Ferris wheels in Japan at 112.5 meters, with a handful of see-through gondolas for views over Osaka Bay.
access: 5-minute walk from Osakako Station (Osaka Metro Chuo Line)

title: Abeno Harukas Observatory
summary: At 300 meters, the tallest building in the Kansai region, with a 300th-floor observatory ("Harukas 300") offering a 360-degree view across the entire city.
access: Directly connected to Tennoji Station (JR Osaka Loop Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Abeno Harukas Harukas 300 observatory tickets

title: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku Tower
summary: A retro downtown district built around a century-old observation tower, where kushikatsu (fried skewer) stalls and old-fashioned pachinko parlors give a rougher, more nostalgic feel than the shinier parts of the city.
access: 3-minute walk from Dobutsuen-mae Station (Osaka Metro Midosuji Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Shinsekai kushikatsu food tour

title: Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine
summary: The head shrine of over 2,000 Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, over 1,800 years old, with a distinctive arched drum bridge at its entrance.
access: 3-minute walk from Sumiyoshi-taisha Station (Nankai Main Line)

title: Shitennoji Temple
summary: One of Japan's oldest officially administered temples, said to have been founded in 593 by Prince Shotoku, with a five-story pagoda rebuilt in its original Asuka-period layout.
access: 5-minute walk from Shitennoji-mae-Yuhigaoka Station (Osaka Metro Tanimachi Line)

title: Tsuruhashi Korea Town
summary: A dense market of around 120 Korean grocers, barbecue restaurants, and cosmetics shops around Tsuruhashi Station, reflecting Osaka's large Korean-Japanese community.
access: 1-minute walk from Tsuruhashi Station (JR Osaka Loop Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Tsuruhashi Korean BBQ food tour

title: Expo '70 Commemorative Park
summary: The former site of the 1970 World Expo, now a large park centered on Taro Okamoto's towering Tower of the Sun sculpture, with seasonal flower fields and a Japanese garden.
access: 15-minute walk from Bampaku-kinen-koen Station (Osaka Monorail), in Suita

affiliateLinks.label: Book Expo '70 Park & Tower of the Sun tickets

title: Minoh Falls
summary: A 33-meter waterfall at the end of a gentle 40-minute forest walk from Minoh town, ranked among Japan's 100 best waterfalls and especially popular for autumn leaves.
access: 40-minute walk from Minoh Station (Hankyu Minoh Line), in Minoh

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Minoh Falls hiking day trip

title: Fushimi Inari Shrine
summary: Thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the mountain — most visitors turn back early, but the upper trail is quiet and forested.
access: 5-minute walk from Inari Station (JR Nara Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Arashiyama & Fushimi Inari day tour

title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
summary: A soaring bamboo forest path, best visited early morning before the crowds arrive.
access: 5-minute walk from Saga-Arashiyama Station (JR Sagano Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Arashiyama bamboo grove tour

title: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
summary: A UNESCO World Heritage temple built without a single nail, whose famous wooden stage juts out over the hillside with sweeping views of the city below.
access: 10-minute walk from Kiyomizu-Gojo Station (Keihan Main Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kiyomizu-dera guided walking tour

title: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka
summary: A pair of connected stone-paved slopes lined with wooden machiya houses turned into tea shops and souvenir stores, leading up to Kiyomizu-dera.
access: 12-minute walk from Kiyomizu-Gojo Station (Keihan Main Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Higashiyama backstreets walking tour

title: Gion & Hanamikoji Street
summary: Kyoto's best-preserved geisha district, where teahouses with wooden latticework line a quiet street — visit at dusk for a chance to spot a geiko or maiko on their way to an appointment.
access: 5-minute walk from Gion-Shijo Station (Keihan Main Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Gion evening walking tour

title: Nishiki Market
summary: Known as "Kyoto's Kitchen," a narrow 390-meter covered arcade of about 130 shops selling pickles, skewered sweets, and knives passed down through generations.
access: 2-minute walk from Shijo Station (Hankyu Kyoto Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Nishiki Market food-tasting tour

title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
summary: A Zen temple pavilion covered in real gold leaf, reflected in a still pond it was purpose-built to overlook — one of Kyoto's most photographed sights.
access: Bus ride from Kyoto Station to the Kinkakuji-michi stop, then a short walk

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kinkaku-ji & northwest Kyoto highlights tour

title: Ryoan-ji Rock Garden
summary: A minimalist Zen rock garden of raked gravel and fifteen stones, arranged so that at least one stone is always hidden from view no matter where you sit.
access: 7-minute walk from Ryoanji-michi bus stop

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji & Ninna-ji day tour

title: Philosopher's Path
summary: A quiet canal-side walking path lined with roughly 400 cherry trees, named after a Kyoto University philosopher who used it for his daily walk to work.
access: Bus ride to the Ginkakuji-michi stop, then a short walk to the northern end of the path

title: Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion)
summary: Despite the name, never actually covered in silver — a restrained wooden pavilion surrounded by meticulously raked sand gardens that inspired the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi.
access: Bus ride to the Ginkakuji-michi stop, then a 10-minute walk

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Higashiyama temples walking tour

title: Heian Shrine
summary: A vividly orange and green shrine complex built in 1895, fronted by one of Japan's largest torii gates, with a large strolling garden behind it that blooms with irises and cherry blossoms in season.
access: 10-minute walk from Higashiyama Station (Kyoto Municipal Subway Tozai Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Find hotels near Okazaki & Heian Shrine

title: Nijo Castle
summary: A UNESCO-listed shogunate castle known for its "nightingale floors," which chirp underfoot as a built-in defense against sneaking intruders.
access: 5-minute walk from Nijojo-mae Station (Kyoto Municipal Subway Tozai Line)

title: Sagano Scenic Railway
summary: A slow open-window sightseeing train running along a retired rail line above the Hozugawa River gorge, especially popular in autumn for the valley's colored leaves.
access: Departs from Torokko Saga Station, next to JR Saga-Arashiyama Station

title: Byodo-in Temple
summary: An 11th-century temple in Uji whose Phoenix Hall is famous enough to appear on the back of the Japanese 10-yen coin, set beside a reflecting pond designed to represent Buddhist paradise.
access: 10-minute walk from Uji Station (JR Nara Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Uji day trip tour with matcha tasting

title: Fushimi Sake District
summary: A canal-side neighborhood of century-old sake breweries built around a natural spring, including a museum brewery where visitors can taste several styles side by side.
access: 7-minute walk from Chushojima Station (Keihan Uji Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Fushimi sake brewery tasting tour

title: Nishijin Textile Center
summary: A working museum for Nishijin-ori, Kyoto's centuries-old woven silk textile craft, with weaving demonstrations and kimono try-on experiences in a quiet neighborhood away from the main sightseeing routes.
access: 3-minute walk from Imadegawa-Horikawa bus stop

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kyoto kimono rental experience

title: Kifune Shrine & Kurama
summary: A mountain shrine dedicated to the god of water, reached via the forested village of Kurama and a hiking trail linking the two — a cooler, quieter escape from central Kyoto in summer.
access: 5-minute walk from Kibuneguchi Station (Eizan Railway), then a short bus or walk

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Kurama & Kibune hiking day tour

title: Tofuku-ji Temple
summary: A large Zen temple with a valley of roughly 2,000 maple trees crossed by a covered wooden bridge, considered one of Kyoto's best autumn foliage spots with noticeably thinner crowds than Kiyomizu-dera.
access: 3-minute walk from Tofukuji Station (JR Nara Line / Keihan Main Line)

title: Sorano Onsen OSAKA BAY TOWER
summary: A hot-spring theme park by the bay with nine different baths, including outdoor tubs with harbor views, plus saunas and a food court for a full half-day visit.
access: 5-minute walk from Bentencho Station (JR Osaka Loop Line)

title: Spa LaQua
summary: A natural hot-spring spa drawn from 1,700 meters underground, inside the Tokyo Dome City complex, with indoor and outdoor baths and a relaxation lounge for resting between soaks.
access: 2-minute walk from Korakuen Station (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi/Namboku Lines)

title: Yasaka Shrine
summary: The shrine at the top of Gion's main street that hosts the Gion Matsuri every July, one of Japan's most famous festivals, with towering wooden floats parading through the city center.
access: Directly adjacent to the Gion-Shijo Station area (Keihan Main Line)

title: Imado Shrine
summary: A small shrine said to be the birthplace of the beckoning cat figurine, popular with visitors hoping for good relationships and matching pairs of cat statues at the altar.
access: 15-minute walk from Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line)

title: Sumida Edo Kiriko Glass
summary: A working studio and shop for Edo kiriko, a centuries-old style of cut glassware, where visitors can watch craftspeople carve patterns by hand and try a short cutting lesson themselves.
access: 10-minute walk from Kinshicho Station (JR Sobu Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Edo kiriko glass-cutting workshop

title: Edo-Tokyo Museum
summary: A museum built around a life-size replica of the Nihonbashi bridge, with detailed scale models recreating how the city looked across four centuries, from Edo-period streets to postwar reconstruction.
access: 3-minute walk from Ryogoku Station (JR Sobu Line)

title: National Museum of Western Art
summary: A UNESCO World Heritage building designed by Le Corbusier, housing Monet, Rodin, and other European masterworks collected by a single Japanese industrialist in the early 20th century.
access: 1-minute walk from Ueno Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book National Museum of Western Art tickets

title: National Museum of Nature and Science
summary: A dinosaur-skeleton-filled science museum in Ueno Park spanning natural history and Japanese scientific achievement, popular with families on rainy days.
access: 5-minute walk from Ueno Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book National Museum of Nature and Science tickets

title: Nezu Shrine
summary: A nearly 1,900-year-old shrine with a tunnel of roughly a hundred small torii gates and an azalea garden that draws crowds every April, without the lines of its more famous counterparts.
access: 5-minute walk from Nezu Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

title: Shibamata Taishakuten
summary: A temple approach street that inspired a decades-long Japanese film series, lined with old rice-cracker shops and dumpling stalls in a part of Tokyo that still feels like a small town.
access: 3-minute walk from Shibamata Station (Keisei Kanamachi Line)

title: Kameido Katori Shrine
summary: A shrine over 1,000 years old dedicated to a god of sports and strength, popular with athletes before competitions and quieter than the shrines nearer the main tourist routes.
access: 8-minute walk from Kameido Station (JR Sobu Line)

title: Tokyo Station & KITTE Marunouchi
summary: A red-brick early-20th-century station building fronting Marunouchi, paired with the KITTE shopping complex next door, whose rooftop garden looks straight down onto the platforms.
access: Directly at Tokyo Station (JR lines)

title: Marunouchi Naka-dori
summary: A tree-lined boulevard of flagship luxury boutiques between Tokyo Station and the Imperial Palace, closed to traffic on weekday lunch hours so office workers can eat outside.
access: 3-minute walk from Tokyo Station (JR lines)

title: Imperial Palace
summary: The residence of Japan's Imperial family, built on the site of the old Edo Castle — the East Gardens are open to the public free of charge, and the outer moat path is a popular running loop.
access: 5-minute walk from Otemachi Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Imperial Palace East Gardens guided tour

title: Kabukiza Theatre
summary: Tokyo's main kabuki theater, where a single-act "hitomaku-mi" ticket lets visitors watch just one scene without committing to a full multi-hour performance.
access: Directly connected to Higashi-Ginza Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

title: Nihombashi Bridge
summary: The historic zero-mile marker for all of Japan's highways, topped with bronze dragon and kirin statues, though currently overshadowed by an elevated expressway slated for removal.
access: 1-minute walk from Nihombashi Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line)

title: AKB48 Theater
summary: A small dedicated theater in Akihabara where the idol group AKB48 performs regular live shows in an intimate room, a different experience from watching them on television.
access: 5-minute walk from Akihabara Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Odaiba Marine Park & Rainbow Bridge
summary: An artificial sand beach facing a replica Statue of Liberty and the illuminated Rainbow Bridge, best visited at dusk as the Tokyo skyline lights up across the bay.
access: 3-minute walk from Odaiba-Kaihinkoen Station (Yurikamome Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book an Odaiba & Tokyo Bay night cruise

title: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza
summary: A bayside shopping mall fronted by a full-scale Gundam robot statue that lights up and moves on the hour, a favorite photo stop even for visitors who aren't shopping.
access: 5-minute walk from Tokyo Teleport Station (Rinkai Line)

title: Immersive Fort Tokyo
summary: A walk-through entertainment park where actors and set design turn visitors into participants in staged mysteries and samurai battles rather than passive spectators.
access: 10-minute walk from Aomi Station (Yurikamome Line)

title: Tokyo Joypolis
summary: An indoor arcade-meets-theme-park run by Sega, packed with VR rides and rhythm games — a good rainy-day option in Odaiba for teens and arcade fans.
access: 3-minute walk from Odaiba-Kaihinkoen Station (Yurikamome Line)

title: Fuji TV Building
summary: A Kenzo Tange-designed broadcasting headquarters with a distinctive titanium sphere suspended between two towers, containing an observation deck over Odaiba.
access: 3-minute walk from Daiba Station (Yurikamome Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Fuji TV Building Hachitama observatory tickets

title: Yakatabune Dinner Cruise
summary: A traditional low-roofed wooden boat dinner cruise around Tokyo Bay, serving tempura and other seasonal courses while the skyline and bridges drift past the windows.
access: Departs from various piers, commonly near Asakusa or Hinode Pier

title: Toyosu Market
summary: Tokyo's relocated central wholesale market, where an elevated public walkway lets early risers watch the famous tuna auction without getting in the way of the trading floor.
access: 7-minute walk from Shijo-mae Station (Yurikamome Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Toyosu Market tuna auction tour

title: Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai
summary: A retro-styled market street built next to Toyosu Market, combining about 70 seafood restaurants and souvenir shops with a hot-spring bathhouse on the upper floor.
access: 7-minute walk from Shijo-mae Station (Yurikamome Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai hot spring admission

title: Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science)
summary: A hands-on science museum built around a giant globe made of LED panels showing real-time Earth data, with humanoid robot demonstrations and space exploration exhibits.
access: 5-minute walk from Telecom Center Station (Yurikamome Line)

title: Small Worlds Tokyo
summary: A miniature-model theme park recreating Tokyo neighborhoods, Kansai International Airport, and anime worlds at 1:80 scale, with tiny trains and cars in constant motion.
access: 3-minute walk from Kokusai-Tenjijo-Seimon Station (Yurikamome Line)

title: Tsukishima Monja Street
summary: A street of roughly 80 restaurants specializing in monjayaki, Tokyo's gooier cousin of okonomiyaki, cooked tableside on a hot iron griddle.
access: 5-minute walk from Tsukishima Station (Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book a Tsukishima monjayaki cooking experience

title: Maxell Aqua Park Shinagawa
summary: An aquarium inside Shinagawa Station that mixes fish tanks with projection mapping and a dolphin show lit up in shifting colors, open into the evening for a date-night option.
access: 2-minute walk from Shinagawa Station (JR Yamanote Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Maxell Aqua Park Shinagawa tickets

title: Haneda Airport Observation Deck
summary: Free rooftop viewing decks across three terminals for watching planes take off, plus an Edo-period-themed food court built to look like an old Tokyo streetscape.
access: Directly at Haneda Airport (Tokyo Monorail / Keikyu Line)

title: Tokyo Tower
summary: An orange-and-white 333-meter lattice tower modeled on the Eiffel Tower, with a glass floor panel on the main deck for looking straight down at the streets below.
access: 5-minute walk from Akabanebashi Station (Tokyo Metro Oedo Line)

affiliateLinks.label: Book Tokyo Tower observation deck tickets

title: Zojoji Temple
summary: The former family temple of the Tokugawa shoguns, whose main gate frames a postcard view of Tokyo Tower rising directly behind it.
access: 3-minute walk from Onarimon Station (Toei Mita Line)

title: National Art Center, Tokyo
summary: Japan's largest exhibition space, with no permanent collection of its own — instead a rotating calendar of major touring shows, inside a wavy glass facade designed by Kisho Kurokawa.
access: 4-minute walk from Nogizaka Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

title: Tokyo Midtown
summary: A mixed-use complex on the former Defense Agency site, known for a large grassy lawn that hosts cherry blossom picnics in spring and an illumination display in winter.
access: Directly connected to Roppongi Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya/Oedo Lines)

title: teamLab Borderless
summary: A digital art museum inside Azabudai Hills with over 70 installations that blend into one another as visitors walk between rooms, so the same piece never looks the same twice.
access: 5-minute walk from Kamiyacho Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

title: National Diet Building
summary: Japan's parliament building, a symmetrical stone structure completed in 1936, with free guided tours through the House of Representatives chamber when it's not in session.
access: 3-minute walk from Kokkai-gijidomae Station (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line)

title: MIYASHITA PARK
summary: A shopping complex built over a former public park, with a 1,000-square-meter rooftop lawn above the stores where people picnic and skateboard within sight of Shibuya's skyline.
access: 3-minute walk from Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Shibuya Sky
summary: An open-air rooftop observation deck 229 meters above Shibuya Scramble Square, with hammock-style seating areas and unobstructed views over the crossing below.
access: Directly connected to Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Shibuya Stream
summary: A riverside redevelopment along a once-hidden stretch of the Shibuya River, now a walkway lined with restaurant terraces that stays lively well after the shops nearby close.
access: Directly connected to Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Cat Street
summary: A curving pedestrian lane connecting Shibuya and Harajuku, lined with streetwear boutiques and independent designers, quieter and more browsable than Takeshita Street nearby.
access: 8-minute walk from Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Omotesando Hills
summary: A sloped, spiral-ramp shopping complex designed by Tadao Ando along Omotesando's tree-lined avenue, built to echo the elevation of the original 1927 apartment block it replaced.
access: 3-minute walk from Meiji-jingumae Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

title: Yoyogi Park
summary: A large open park next to Meiji Jingu that fills with street performers, picnickers, and food festivals most weekends, and turns into one of Tokyo's liveliest cherry blossom spots each spring.
access: 3-minute walk from Harajuku Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Ebisu Garden Place
summary: A quiet plaza built on the site of an old beer brewery, home to a small photography museum and a free-to-enter observation lounge with skyline views from a nearby tower.
access: 5-minute walk from Ebisu Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory
summary: A free observation deck 202 meters up in Tokyo's city hall towers, offering a view of Mount Fuji on clear winter days without paying for a ticket anywhere else.
access: 8-minute walk from Shinjuku Station (JR Yamanote Line)

title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
summary: A large garden combining French formal, English landscape, and traditional Japanese garden styles in one park, considered one of Tokyo's best cherry blossom spots.
access: 10-minute walk from Shinjuku-gyoenmae Station (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line)

title: Kabukicho
summary: Tokyo's largest entertainment district, a dense grid of neon signs, bars, and theaters — best explored with a guide who knows which alleys are worth a look and which to skip.
access: 3-minute walk from Shinjuku Station (JR Yamanote Line)
